skill.name: data-visualization
skill.description: Create charts, graphs, and visual reports from structured data using common Python visualization libraries.
skill.summary: Guide chart creation, styling, and export for clear data visualizations.
skill.author: 0xkynz

security_audit.summary: The only static finding points to a Python code fence in SKILL.md, not Ruby or shell execution. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or command execution intent was found in the reviewed skill text.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md lines 14-21 contain a fenced Python matplotlib example. It plots hardcoded arrays and saves chart.png; there is no shell execution or user-controlled command.

content.value_statement: Data often hides trends when it stays in tables. This skill guides chart selection, styling, and export for clear visual reports.
actual_capabilities: Recommends chart types such as line charts, bar charts, pie charts, scatter plots, histograms, box plots, and heatmaps.
Guides use of Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, and Altair for static, statistical, interactive, and declarative visualizations.
Supports planning for multi-axis plots, subplot grids, custom themes, annotations, and labels.
Helps prepare exports for PNG, SVG, and PDF output formats.
Provides basic chart examples for quick visualization setup.
limitations: It does not include executable scripts or reusable chart components.
It depends on the host environment having the selected visualization library installed.
It does not validate source data quality before chart design.
It provides guidance, not automated dashboard hosting or live data refresh.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Business Trend Chart
use_cases.description: Turn sales, usage, or operations data into a labeled chart for a stakeholder report.

use_cases.title: Explore a Dataset Visually
use_cases.description: Choose charts that reveal distributions, relationships, and outliers during analysis.

use_cases.title: Create Presentation Graphics
use_cases.description: Design clean static visuals with accessible colors, readable labels, and export-ready resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this dataset: [describe columns and goal]. Recommend the best chart type and explain why it fits.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Static Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Matplotlib or Seaborn plan for this data: [data summary]. Include title, axes, labels, colors, and export format.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Visualization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chart description: [chart details]. Suggest improvements for readability, accessibility, labeling, and focus.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Panel Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a visualization report for [business question]. Include chart types, subplot layout, annotations, and final export recommendations.

output_examples.input: Monthly revenue by product category for one year.
output_examples.output: A grouped bar chart plan with clear category colors, month labels, revenue axis formatting, and PNG export guidance.

output_examples.input: Customer age, signup channel, purchase count, and churn status.
output: Stacked bar chart for churn by signup channel.
Scatter plot for purchase count against age.

output_examples.input: Weekly support tickets, average response time, and satisfaction score.
output_examples.output: A multi-axis trend chart plan with annotations for major incidents and separate color treatment for each metric.

best_practices: Select the chart type that matches the question, not only the data shape.
Use clear titles, axis labels, legends, and annotations where they reduce confusion.
Check color contrast and export resolution before sharing the final chart.
anti_patterns: Do not use pie charts for many categories or small differences.
Do not overload one chart with unrelated metrics and competing scales.
Do not omit labels, units, or context needed to interpret the visualization.

faq.question: Which libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly, and Altair for common visualization workflows.

faq.question: Can it create interactive charts?
faq.answer: It can guide Plotly and Altair chart plans, including interactive use cases when supported by the environment.

faq.question: Does it run chart code automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides instructions and examples, but the user or agent must run code in an appropriate environment.

faq.question: What chart formats can it help export?
faq.answer: It can help prepare exports such as PNG, SVG, and PDF, depending on the selected library.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes readable labels, simple layouts, and color choices that support accessible interpretation.

faq.question: Is it suitable for dashboards?
faq.answer: It can plan dashboard visuals, but it does not provide hosting, data refresh, or dashboard application code.
